adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), when sanitized != value it computes `start` as the length of the common prefix and `end` as the length of the common suffix independently, then calls `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)`. There is no guard that `start <= value.length()-end` (or for sanitized). For cases where one string is a strict prefix of the other (e.g., value="aaaaa", sanitized="aaaa"), the loops can yield `start=4` and `end=4`, making `value.substring(4, 1)` and throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the diff. This behavior is directly implied by the added loops in the diff.

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties.java, HTML_TAGS is defined as Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>") and ANCHOR_PATTERN as Pattern.compile("]*>"). Both only match lowercase tag names. verifySafeHtml() uses containsHtml(englishValue) (driven by HTML_TAGS) to choose between POLICY_SOME_HTML vs POLICY_NO_HTML, and santizeAnchors() (driven by ANCHOR_PATTERN) to allow only source anchors. If the English string contains uppercase/mixed-case tags like "
" or "", containsHtml() will incorrectly return false (thus disallowing HTML), and santizeAnchors() may fail to match/validate anchors, while the OWASP sanitizer will still treat and strip/normalize those tags case-insensitively. This can produce spurious "Illegal HTML" or "Didn't find anchor tag" messages for otherwise legitimate content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P3 | misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:75 | The locale-suffix character class in `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` excludes digits, so a properties filename whose locale/variant segment contains a digit (e.g. an "_es_419"-style suffix) fails to match; the replaceAll is then a no-op and `englishFile` resolves back to the translation file itself, silently comparing the file against itself and skipping all HTML verification for that locale instead of failing loudly. | correctness | 35 |

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English bundle path is derived via `.replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. That character class excludes digits, so filenames with digit-containing locale/variant segments (e.g. `_es_419.properties`) will not match and the suffix replacement becomes a no-op. For files not under `resources-community` (or after the first replacement is irrelevant), this can make `englishFile` equal the translation file path, causing `bundleEnglish` to load the same file and defeating the intended "only allow HTML if English contains HTML" check for that locale. This is a real correctness defect in the new HTML verification logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:150-162 | `santizeAnchors()` matches anchor tags strictly in sequential order between `value` and `englishValue` (pairing the Nth `matcher.find()` with the Nth `englishMatcher.find()`); if a translation contains two or more anchors and legitimately reorders them relative to the English source (valid word-order differences between languages), distinct-but-valid anchors get paired against each other, causing a false "Didn't find anchor tag" report even though the anchor set is unchanged. | correctness | 40 |

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors()`, each ``/`` tag found in `value` is compared only against the next tag found in `englishValue` via `englishMatcher.find()` (i.e., Nth-to-Nth sequential pairing) and requires `Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())`. If a translation legitimately reorders multiple anchors relative to English (same tags but different order), the first mismatched pair will trigger `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag ...")` even though the tag exists later in `englishValue`. This creates false failures in the verifier logic introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds build-time HTML validation in `verifySafeHtml()` and then post-processes the sanitizer output with `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` and `sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")`. POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML;`. Since `POLICY_SOME_HTML` allows `br`, `p`, `strong`, and `b` elements, any key whose English string contains any HTML tag (as detected by `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`) will permit translators to add those allowed tags anywhere in the translation, not just mirroring where English had HTML. This is a real, diff-grounded permissiveness/integrity concern, but given the allowed tags are limited and attributes are not allowed by the policy builder, it’s more a policy/scope issue than a clear functional/security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P0 | misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:92-99 | Empirically verified against the pinned owasp-java-html-sanitizer 20240325.1: for input `Hello {{constructor.constructor('alert(1)')()}} world`, `policy.sanitize()` defangs the template-injection pattern by inserting its own `{<!-- -->{...}` HTML-comment split (a documented anti-mustache/Angular-sandbox-escape defense with no real HTML tags involved), but the code's own `unescapeHtml4(...)` + `.replace("<!-- -->", "")` post-processing exactly and deterministically reconstructs the original byte-for-byte string, so `sanitized.equals(value)` is true and no "Illegal HTML" message is ever emitted for this payload under either POLICY_SOME_HTML or POLICY_NO_HTML. | adversarial | 65 |

adjudication.rationale: In verifySafeHtml(), the sanitizer output is post-processed with `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` and then `sanitized = sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")`. The code comment explicitly acknowledges the OWASP sanitizer may insert `<!-- -->` “when there are double curly braces”. Removing that marker can undo the sanitizer’s defensive transformation and make `sanitized` equal to the original `value`, so the tool will not report it as illegal even though the sanitizer tried to modify/defang it. This is a verifiable bypass of the verifier’s intended “sanitized must match original” check for such payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:145,150-162 | `ANCHOR_PATTERN` (`</?a[^>]*>`) is lowercase-only, so an uppercase/mixed-case anchor such as `<A HREF="http://malicious.com">` is invisible to `santizeAnchors()` and never triggers its specific "Didn't find anchor tag" message; however this is only a diagnostic degradation, not a full silent-pass — verified empirically that the OWASP sanitizer still recognizes the tag case-insensitively and strips it under both policies (neither allows `a`), so the generic `Illegal HTML` diff check at line 99 still fires for the mismatch. | adversarial | 80 |

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ANCHOR_PATTERN` is `Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>")` with no `CASE_INSENSITIVE` flag, so mixed/upper-case anchors like `<A ...>` will not be matched by `santizeAnchors()`. As a result, such anchors won’t trigger the specific "Didn't find anchor tag" diagnostic, and won’t be stripped by `santizeAnchors()` when they are equivalent to the English string. This is a real, diff-grounded edge case affecting anchor-handling/diagnostics, but it doesn’t obviously create a silent pass in this verifier because later sanitization + comparison can still report an issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:99-111 | `verify()`'s catch block only handles `IOException` and the per-key `forEachRemaining` lambda in `verifySafeHtml()` has no exception handling of its own; the prefix/suffix trim loops at 102-109 never clamp `start + end` to `Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length())` before the `substring` calls at line 111, so a value/sanitized pair with self-overlapping repeated characters at both ends could throw an uncaught `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` that aborts checking of all remaining keys in that file with no messages recorded for them; I was not able to construct a concrete real sanitizer output that overflows this bound within the time available, so this needs further verification rather than being a confirmed live exploit. | adversarial | 40 |

adjudication.rationale: In `verifySafeHtml()`, when `sanitized != value` it computes `start` (common prefix length) and `end` (common suffix length) independently, then calls `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` / `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` without ensuring `start <= (len - end)` for each string. If one string is a strict prefix/suffix of the other (e.g., `value="a"`, `sanitized="aa"`), `start` can reach `value.length()` while `end` can also be `value.length()`, making `value.length() - end == 0` and `start == 1`, causing `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. There is no local exception handling in the per-key iteration, so this would abort checking remaining keys in that file.
